title: Reason Code 66 — authentication method not enabled on the matched policy
plain_english: A network policy matched, but the client tried to authenticate with a method that policy doesn't allow. Client and server each did their job — they just don't agree on HOW to authenticate. The event's 'Authentication Type' and 'EAP Type' fields versus the policy's constraints tell the whole story.

any: authentication method that is not enabled on the matching network policy

causes.cause: EAP method mismatch — the device requests PEAP-MSCHAPv2 while the policy only lists EAP-TLS (typical mid-migration), or vice versa.
causes.next_check: Compare this event's 'EAP Type' with the EAP types in the policy's Constraints → Authentication Methods; add the method or fix the client profile.

causes.cause: The client fell back to a non-EAP method (PAP/CHAP/MS-CHAPv2 without EAP) that is unchecked in the policy — common with wired 802.1X fallbacks and VPN profiles.
causes.next_check: Look at 'Authentication Type' in the event: if it isn't EAP, decide deliberately whether to enable that method (weakens security) or fix the client.

causes.cause: The request matched a DIFFERENT policy than you intended, one with stricter methods.
causes.next_check: Check 'Network Policy Name' in this event — if it's not the policy you expected, fix conditions/ordering rather than adding methods to the wrong policy.
